source.title: PAC-Bayesian Generalization Bounds for Knowledge Graph Representation Learning
source.authors: Jaejun Lee; Minsung Hwang; Joyce Jiyoung Whang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures generalization errors while varying graph aggregation, weight-matrix norms, encoder depth, and representation dimension in knowledge-graph models. This is an extension to a different task and setting; it does not test the specified versions directly.
record.gate_note: The study defines generalization error as the observed difference between expected and empirical losses. Its experiments report trends for several model factors, but none directly test the conditions named by V1–V8. Theoretical bounds and cited prior-work results are not extracted as experimental rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives bounds and measures generalization gaps for knowledge-graph triplet classifiers, but its results test none of V1–V8. Representation-dimension sweeps do not establish post-interpolation test-error behavior (V2), and Gaussian perturbations used in proofs do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of gaps (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the bounds provide theoretical grounds for parameter sharing, weight normalization, and mean aggregation. Experiments show predicted gap trends for aggregation, matrix norms, depth, and dimension; parameter sharing is not experimentally tested.
record.recipe_differences: Develops transductive PAC-Bayesian bounds for knowledge-graph triplet classification and evaluates selected bound factors on real-world knowledge graphs; it does not reproduce the original methods in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Generalization error changes with aggregation choice, weight-matrix norm, encoder depth, and maximum representation dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean aggregation yields smaller reported gaps than sum aggregation; gaps increase with fixed matrix norms, encoder depth, and representation dimension. The gap compares full-set classification loss with training-set margin loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested ReED knowledge-graph configurations, aggregation, weight normalization, depth, and representation dimension affect the observed classification-versus-margin generalization gap in directions predicted by the bounds.

record.problems: The experimental evidence is reported mainly as trends in figures; precise generalization-error values are not stated in the text. The experiments cover three knowledge graphs and the studied ReED configurations, not the image-classification or language settings in the versions.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying experimental results were omitted. Theoretical bound derivations and cited prior-work findings are not rows because they are not experimental outcomes from this study.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes; Adam is used without an optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Empirical magnitude-aware sharpness, correlation with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equal-size random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The rows' stated directional findings are supported. Their cannot_determine states concern V1–V8 applicability, not whether those unrelated trends were observed. Neither a larger generalization gap nor a looser upper bound alone establishes worse held-out accuracy.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; no random-label comparison.
No one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep across the interpolation threshold on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD under tuning regimes.
The study varies graph aggregation, weight norms, depth, and representation dimension; it does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare sharpness measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: ReED (RAMP+TD and RAMP+SM; aggregate across all datasets and models)
rows.operation_detail: Compared generalization error using mean versus sum aggregation, controlling the other measured factors.
rows.measure: Generalization error (difference between expected and empirical losses)
rows.value: mean aggregator showed lower generalization errors across all datasets and all models
rows.uncertainty: Experiments repeated 10 times; mean and standard deviation visualized, numerical values not stated.
rows.note: Aggregate direction is stated in text; individual dataset/model values are shown in Figure 2.
rows.check: The reported mean-versus-sum trend is supported, but measures no claim version. FB15K237 and CoDEx-M are sampled subsets. Specify that the gap compares full-set classification loss with training-set margin loss.

rows.subject: ReED (RAMP+TD and RAMP+SM; aggregate across all datasets and models)
rows.operation_detail: Varied the maximum Frobenius norm s of learnable matrices, normalizing each weight matrix after each backpropagation step.
rows.measure: Generalization error (difference between expected and empirical losses)
rows.value: Generalization errors increase as s increases.
rows.uncertainty: Experiments repeated 10 times; mean and standard deviation visualized, numerical values not stated.
rows.note: The reported trend aggregates across datasets and models.
rows.check: The norm trend is supported but does not measure V7 sharpness. Each matrix's Frobenius norm is fixed to s after every update; s is not merely a maximum permitted norm. FB15K237 and CoDEx-M are sampled subsets.
